chapter: California, Art Tatum and Lionel Hampton
title: Sonny Howard's private parties in Los Angeles
summary: Thompson lived with businessman Sonny Howard, whose parties drew Art Tatum, Nat Cole and Eddie Beal to play for their own people.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: I heard Art Tatum as the other people heard him, playing as I said in these jam sessions. All musicians at that time liked to play jazz music played every chance they got. Any place there was a piano, a piano player sat down and played, and some other guys joined him, and they all kinds of places where it was known to be a headquarters for musicians to have these jam sessions. And Art Tatum was at that. Not only that, but I lived with a very, very wonderful man and his wife who always had these little private parties. Now these were different than house rent parties, these were personal parties given by this man who was a businessman. And he loved music, and he loved musicians and entertainers. All the people went to his house. His name was Sonny Howard.
One of the finest gentlemen I ever met in my life, you know.

And the man became like a father to me, a brother. And I stayed at his house, and this is where Art Tatum and all of the great musicians, Nat Cole, Eddie Beal Bill, another fine pianist, all -- everybody came there every night for these little private parties that he had for people. It was just -- this was -- because this was where everyone could come and relax and have a few drinks, and the musicians felt that they were in their own home, in their own society, and everybody felt like playing because there wasn't anybody in there that didn't understand it. And they were playing for their own people --
Ahh, I didn't know you knew what that word meant.
There are too many drags not to know the word.
No, some people won't know how to interpret that, so we'll keep that for our secret.
These sessions that Sonny Howard's, which must have been very marvelous, what else -- who else came to them, and did you make up a friendship with Art Tatum at that time?
Very definitely. In fact this has to be the most serious point of my career, and where I really got the

right kind of guidance from Art Tatum as well as many others, particularly Art Tatum. As I said, in this house, these professionals who were then successful people, came there and played every night. Art Tatum just happened to be the star, and the fact of the matter is Art would sit around and drink a little beer and talk. He was very intellectual, very kind gentleman. And most all of the other pianists would come in and play. King Cole would come in and play and he'd sing. And a fine pianist by the name of Eddie Beale. He would play. And any other pianist who came in and felt like playing played.
